meta.caveat: Architecture-first seed for UI; not claimed ladder-optimal. Scores describe species/form tendencies across plausible Champions doubles architectures rather than one exact set.
meta.scale: All numeric scores are integers 0–5 unless noted. 0 = absent, 3 = solid, 5 = elite for Champions doubles architectures.

metricDefs.label: Engine Participation Count
metricDefs.meaning: How many distinct win engines / infrastructure loops this species can meaningfully participate in across common Champions doubles architectures, rather than within only one team.

metricDefs.label: Engine Exclusivity Tax
metricDefs.meaning: How often teammates must become dedicated servants for this species to function. High tax means packages collapse around it; low tax means many packages can support it lightly.

metricDefs.label: Bridge Quality
metricDefs.meaning: How effectively this species participates in separate modules without forcing either module to compromise.

metricDefs.label: Create Fan-Out
metricDefs.meaning: How many strategically distinct teammate roles can consume what this species creates.

metricDefs.label: Convert Fan-Out
metricDefs.meaning: How many distinct infrastructure forms this species can convert into progress, such as weather, Tailwind, Fake Out turns, terrain, Intimidate turns, screens, Trick Room, redirection, or free setup turns.

metricDefs.label: MAG
metricDefs.meaning: Marginal Architecture Gain — how much genuinely new strategic territory this species tends to open on Champions doubles sixes at species baseline rather than in one specific six.

metricDefs.label: Module Elasticity Support
metricDefs.meaning: As a root or key module, how many strategically different packages it can support without rebuilding the six.

metricDefs.label: Engine-Converter Continuity
metricDefs.meaning: How effectively this species can create a favorable resource or state and later personally convert that same state into damage, control, scaling, or a win condition instead of requiring another dedicated converter.

teamContextRules.cMagHint: Start with species-baseline MAG, then inspect the five teammates for duplicated territory. Raise C-MAG when the candidate adds a genuinely new engine, failure condition, speed state, damage axis, counterplay inversion, Mega package, or conversion route that existing teammates can also exploit. Lower C-MAG when it merely strengthens an already-saturated route without creating a meaningfully different package or failure state.
teamContextRules.exclusivityGivenSix: Lower Engine Exclusivity Tax when the other five already provide the infrastructure this species wants while remaining useful in unrelated packages. Lower it further when the species can function autonomously after consuming that infrastructure. Raise it when several teammates must change moves, items, Mega choice, positioning, speed profiles, or normal roles primarily to enable this species. Shared infrastructure with multiple consumers lowers tax; dedicated servants raise it.
teamContextRules.saturation: Adding another member of the same archetype lowers C-MAG when both create or consume the same resources, compete for the same setup or Mega turn, fail to the same counterplay, or improve the same packages without opening new ones. Functional redundancy remains valuable when the new species converts shared infrastructure differently, creates another speed or damage state, supplies a different endgame, or turns the first route's counterplay into progress for a second route.

profiles.name: Politoed
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Politoed is strongest when Rain is a shared team resource rather than a one-partner activation button.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Moderate personal conversion; its architectural value is mostly elite Rain Fan-Out.
antiPatterns: Building Rain around only one Swift Swim consumer

profiles.name: Primarina
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Primarina is easy to slot because it can convert several speed states and weather without asking the team to become dedicated support.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: High Fan-In with low servant tax and useful Water/Fairy role compression.
antiPatterns: Forcing one speed mode when Primarina can function in several

profiles.name: Mega Pyroar
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Mega Pyroar's graph points inward: it is more valuable as a light-support conversion piece than as an engine root.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: High Fan-In from Sun, speed control, and generic tempo.
antiPatterns: Building a full Sun shell solely for Pyroar

profiles.name: Raichu
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Base Raichu is one of the cleanest low-tax connectors because Fake Out and Lightning Rod create resources for many unrelated packages.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Better personal Fan-In than pure supports because Electric boosts and speed control can become its own damage.
antiPatterns: Using Fake Out without a specific conversion target

profiles.name: Alolan Raichu
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Alolan Raichu is a terrain conversion specialist rather than a broad support Raichu.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Excellent Fan-In when terrain already has several consumers, but higher tax when terrain exists only for Raichu.
antiPatterns: Adding Electric Terrain solely to activate Surge Surfer

profiles.name: Mega Raichu X
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: The critical value is phase transition: Raichu can contribute infrastructure before committing the Mega slot, then become an attacker.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: High ECC and low exclusivity because its support phase benefits many teammates independently.
antiPatterns: Mega evolving before Lightning Rod or Fake Out has purchased useful board value

profiles.name: Mega Raichu Y
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Mega Raichu Y is one of the clearest engine-becomes-converter species: support before Mega, autonomous offense after Mega.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Elite on both axes with almost no servant tax; the same slot can create tempo, protect partners, and later become the clock.
antiPatterns: Mega evolving automatically on turn one
Treating Fake Out as the entire reason to bring Raichu

profiles.name: Rillaboom
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Rillaboom is an elite engine hub because Terrain, Fake Out, priority, recovery, Ground suppression, and pivoting all feed different packages.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Elite ECC: it creates Terrain and immediately converts it itself while simultaneously enabling other converters.
antiPatterns: Treating Rillaboom as only a Fake Out user
Using Terrain with no meaningful secondary consumers

profiles.name: Mega Sableye
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Its create-web can be excellent, but Mega opportunity cost rises sharply if disruption does not feed several independent clocks.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Low personal Fan-In compared with premier offensive Megas.
antiPatterns: Using the Mega slot for disruption without multiple teammates converting the denied turns

profiles.name: Salamence
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Salamence passes the connector test before it attacks: Intimidate, Tailwind, Ground immunity, Dragon control, and credible Mega pressure connect otherwise separate packages without demanding servants.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Its inward graph is also elite because Salamence can personally spend Intimidate-created safety, Tailwind, Fake Out turns, and the Mega slot.
antiPatterns: Building a six that only works if Salamence Mega evolves every game
Treating Intimidate as passive value instead of setup access

profiles.name: Mega Salamence
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Mega Salamence preserves Salamence's elite bridge graph while adding a genuine autonomous conversion phase, so the Mega slot amplifies rather than replaces its connector value.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Elite ECC: pre-Mega Intimidate creates the board, Tailwind reshapes speed, and Mega Salamence can then personally cash those states into damage.
antiPatterns: Mega evolving before pre-Mega Intimidate has generated value
Using Tailwind as a rote move when immediate damage already converts the turn

profiles.name: Mega Sceptile
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Mega Sceptile has better bridge value than a pure fast attacker because Lightning Rod can protect entire Water or Flying modules.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: High Fan-In with low exclusivity; its Electric interaction can itself become infrastructure.
antiPatterns: Using Lightning Rod protection when no partner meaningfully benefits

profiles.name: Scizor
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Scizor converts generic setup access efficiently and retains a strong priority endgame even after external speed control expires.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: High Fan-In, low servant tax when priority is independently useful.
antiPatterns: Using Swords Dance when Bullet Punch already closes the clock

profiles.name: Mega Scizor
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Mega Scizor's value is less about creating team infrastructure and more about turning several generic defensive resources into a self-sustaining priority clock.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Excellent Fan-In and low tax; priority reduces dependence on speed engines.
antiPatterns: Adding redundant speed support when priority already solves the intended endgame

profiles.name: Mega Scolipede
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Mega Scolipede's architecture is mostly inward conversion, but high natural speed keeps support tax manageable.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Strong Fan-In from generic tempo with limited outward creation.
antiPatterns: Using multiple support slots to solve problems its natural speed already handles

profiles.name: Mega Scovillain
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Its dual offensive typing lets shared Sun infrastructure create more matchup reach than a simple Fire sweeper.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: High Fan-In; strongest when Sun already feeds multiple team members.
antiPatterns: Building Sun only to activate Scovillain

profiles.name: Mega Scrafty
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Mega Scrafty scores well because Intimidate and Fake Out remain valuable across many packages before it becomes a slow physical converter.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Strong ECC with low exclusivity; support phase and attack phase occupy the same slot.
antiPatterns: Mega evolving before Intimidate or Fake Out has generated useful infrastructure

profiles.name: Mega Sharpedo
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Sharpedo has thin outward Fan-Out but exceptional ECC because its own pre-Mega speed engine powers the post-Mega converter.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: A pure inward architecture can still be efficient when the activation cost is largely self-contained.
antiPatterns: Adding redundant speed infrastructure instead of exploiting Speed Boost

profiles.name: Sinistcha
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Sinistcha is an unusually high-value connector because simply entering the field creates a reusable resource that many unrelated packages can spend.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Good ECC through pivot-heal loops and slow-board conversion.
antiPatterns: Using Hospitality healing without a pivot structure that can repeat it

profiles.name: Mega Skarmory
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Mega Skarmory can bridge speed control, defensive anchoring, and Ground immunity without forcing a narrow package.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Moderate personal conversion, elite outward graph.
antiPatterns: Using it as passive defense without a clock or setup route

profiles.name: Mega Slowbro
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Mega Slowbro is strongest when Trick Room is both a resource it creates and one several teammates, including Slowbro itself, can spend.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Excellent ECC for a slow Mega; its own durability can manufacture the turns needed to establish the engine.
antiPatterns: Using Trick Room only for Slowbro
Building a passive shell with no second slow converter

profiles.name: Sneasler
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Sneasler is more than a terrain servant because multiple sets can self-activate or consume unrelated infrastructure.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Elite ECC when item consumption is generated by its own moves; very high Fan-In otherwise.
antiPatterns: Assuming Sneasler requires a terrain setter
Over-supporting Unburden when self-activation is available

profiles.name: Mega Staraptor
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Mega Staraptor is one of the closest alternatives to Salamence as a true bridge Mega: Intimidate and Tailwind create resources before its own physical conversion begins.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Elite ECC with almost no servant tax; support and breaker identities coexist naturally.
antiPatterns: Treating Staraptor as only an attacker
Mega evolving before Intimidate value is secured

profiles.name: Mega Starmie
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Mega Starmie can consume multiple unrelated offensive infrastructures, making it more architecture-flexible than a simple fast special attacker.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: High Fan-In, low servant tax, moderate create-web.
antiPatterns: Forcing both Rain and Psychic Terrain onto one six solely for Starmie

profiles.name: Mega Steelix
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Mega Steelix has multiple legitimate infrastructures to consume, but its low speed raises tax unless those infrastructures already serve other teammates.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Good slow-board Fan-In; architecture improves sharply when Sand or Trick Room has several consumers.
antiPatterns: Adding both Sand and Trick Room solely for Steelix

profiles.name: Swampert
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Swampert's low exclusivity comes from functioning across Rain, Tailwind, and slower balance without requiring any one state.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Broad Fan-In plus useful defensive bridge typing.
antiPatterns: Treating Swampert as Rain-only

profiles.name: Mega Swampert
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Mega Swampert is a very powerful weather converter, but its architecture is healthiest when Rain also powers Archaludon, Pelipper, Water pressure, or Fire mitigation.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Elite Rain Fan-In with moderate weather exclusivity.
antiPatterns: Making Rain exist only for Mega Swampert

profiles.name: Torkoal
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Torkoal is one of the strongest ECC weather setters because the same Sun that supports the team immediately amplifies its own offense.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Elite create and convert Fan-Out; low tax when Trick Room and Sun have multiple independent consumers.
antiPatterns: Using hard Trick Room only to enable Torkoal
Making every damage route weather-dependent

profiles.name: Tyranitar
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Tyranitar's Sand engine is unusually strong because the setter is also a substantial independent attacker and weather-control piece.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Excellent ECC: it creates Sand, benefits personally, and can turn weather replacement into immediate teammate conversion.
antiPatterns: Leading Tyranitar automatically when preserving weather overwrite is more valuable
Treating Sand as the identity of every Tyranitar team

profiles.name: Mega Tyranitar
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Mega Tyranitar keeps the Sand root while becoming an even more autonomous converter, so the Mega slot strengthens rather than substitutes for its engine role.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Elite ECC and broad Fan-In from Trick Room, Fake Out, weather exchange, and chip.
antiPatterns: Mega evolving when another Mega package has higher matchup value
Forcing Sand after the opponent has already solved the weather route

profiles.name: Venusaur
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Venusaur is more than a Sun converter because sleep itself becomes infrastructure that several teammates can spend.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: High Fan-In with meaningful create Fan-Out through sleep control.
antiPatterns: Treating Sun as mandatory in every Venusaur package
Using sleep without a plan to convert the denied action

profiles.name: Mega Venusaur
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Mega Venusaur exchanges Chlorophyll conversion for a much more autonomous durable-control identity with excellent bridge utility.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: High Fan-In from generic defensive infrastructure with low exclusivity.
antiPatterns: Building Sun automatically when Mega evolution removes the reason Sun was needed

profiles.name: Mega Victreebel
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Mega Victreebel has high conversion Fan-In but a thinner outward graph than premier weather roots.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Strong Sun and tempo consumer with moderate support tax.
antiPatterns: Building Sun exclusively around Victreebel

profiles.name: Whimsicott
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Whimsicott is an elite create-web species because priority Tailwind and special amplification can feed many unrelated converters without demanding package commitment.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Personal damage conversion is secondary, but its infrastructure has exceptional Fan-Out and nearly zero exclusivity.
antiPatterns: Clicking Tailwind automatically when the opponent's speed answer makes another resource more valuable
Pairing Whimsicott with attackers that cannot meaningfully spend its speed or debuff turns
